condition: subacute smooth firm 1 cm dorsal right wrist ganglion lump aching mildly on wrist extension over 6 weeks
level_rationale: Six weeks of a smooth firm 1 cm lump on the back of the right wrist that aches mildly when bending the wrist back in a 27-year-old adult who carries trays describes a classic subacute dorsal wrist ganglion presentation warranting a routine outpatient physician visit for physical examination, confirmation of benign cystic etiology, and conservative or aspiration guidance rather than unguided self-care alone or emergency care, whereas 10 minutes of mild stiffness on the back of the right wrist yesterday right after carrying trays represents transient occupational wrist fatigue needing only routine home self-care.

design_note: Three atomic reference facts cover age 27, carrying trays, and a 6-week smooth firm 1 cm lump on the back of the right wrist aching mildly on wrist extension without naming ganglion or using contractions, with a 2-word span difference (21 vs 23 words) and clean 2x2 crossing.
